turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm listening, Hale. It's 4:15 and I have a call at 4:40, so start with who decided to give Owen a zero.
I'm not upset, Hale. I'm asking you a question. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
But I'm not changing the grade.
Then tell me what it rests on, Hale. Procedure 4.2 says a parent is contacted before any mark is entered, and nobody called me. Owen found out from his phone, in the middle of class.
I'm still not changing it. Keep going if you like.
I'm writing that down, Hale: "I'm still not changing it." Then tell me what the zero is based on, because if you have nothing, my next stop is the principal's office.
You can say it ten more ways. The answer is no.
"The answer is no." Noted, Hale, with no reason attached to it. Then the principal gets that today, and I'll want the zero and your reasons in an email before I leave this room.
